Indian Standard 

METHODS OF TEST FOR 
PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS 

IP : 128] 

DETERMINATION OF NICKEL IN CALCINED PETROLEUM COKE 

( First Reprint AUGUST 1997 ) 
UDC 665-6/7 : 665'777-4-046-41 : 543 [ 54674 ] 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This Indian Standard describes an analytical 
procedure for the determination of nickel in 
calcined petroleum coke. 

2. APPARATUS 

2.1 Volumetric Flasks — 1 OOO-ml, 500-ml, 
250-ml, and 100-mI capacities. 

2.2 Pipettes — 25-ml, 10-ml and lOrml capaci- 
ties. 

2.3 Measaring Cylinders — 100-ml and lO-ml 
capacities. 

2.4 Porcelain Dish — 250-ml capacity. 

2.5 MoflBle Furnace — Capable of controlling 
the temperature between 600 and 1 000^*0 with 
regulator. 

2.6 Spectrophotometer — UV visible. 

3. REAGENTS 

3.1 Dimethylglyoxime Solution ( 1 Percent ) 

— Dissolve 1 g of the above reagent in 100 ml 
of ethyl alcohol. 

3.2 Citric Acid ( 10 Percent Solution ) — 

Dissolve 10 g of citric acid ( CgHg07.H20 ) in 
100 ml of distilled water. 

3.3 Potassium Persulphate ( 2 Percent 

Solution) — Dissolve 2 g of potassium per- 
sulphate ( K2S2O8 ) in 100 ml of distilled water 
( freshly prepared ). 

3.4 Sodium Hydroxide Solution ( 2M ) — 
Dissolve 8 g of NaOH pellets in 50 ml of water, 
cool and make up to 100 ml with distilled water. 

3.5 Nitric Acid Solution ( 8N } — Dilute 
500 ml of HNO3 ( sp gr 1 42 ) to I litre with 
distilled water. 

3.6 Hydrochloride Acid Solution (IN) 

3.7 Sodium Carbonate, Anhydrous 

3.8 Boric Acid 



4. STANDARD NICKEL SOLUTION 

4.1 Preparation of Standard Nickel Solution 

( 1 ml == 0-1 mg Ni) — Dissolve 01 g of pure 
nickel metal ( 99 99 percent ) in 10 ml water and 
5 ml nitric acid in a beaker. When the dissolu- 
tion is complete, boil the solution to remove the 
lower oxides of the nitrogen. Cool and make 
up to 1 000 ml in volumetric flask with distilled 
water and mix. Transfer the contents to 500-ml 
polyethylene bottle tightly covered. 

4.2 Preparation of Standard Nickel Solu- 
tion ( 1 ml = 0-005 mg Ni ) — Dilute 25 ml 
of the stock solution ( see 4.1 ) in a 500-ml 
volumetric flask and make up to the mark with 
distilled water and mix. Transfer the contents to 
500-ml polyethylene bottle having tight fitting 
stopper. 

4.3 Preparation of Calibration Curve 

4.3.1 Transfer 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 ml aliquots of 
standard nickel solution ( 1 ml = 0*005 mg Ni ) 
( see 4.2 ) into 100-ml beakers. Add 5 ml citric 
acid to each beaker and neutralize each solution 
using litmus paper by ammonia (1:1) and add 
5 ml excess. Transfer the solution to a clean 
separating funnel and dilute to 50-70 ml with 
distilled water. Introduce 10 ml dimethylgly- 
oxime solution and mix. Extract with three 5-ml 
portions of chloroform ( CHCI3 ) shaking vigor- 
ously ( 1-2 minutes ) each time and combine the 
chloroform layers in a clean separatory funnel. 
Shake the combined chloroform extract with 
20 ml of 0*5 M ammonia and draw off the 
chloroform layer into another clean separatory 
funnel. Shake the ammoniacal aqueous phase 
with 5 ml of chloroform. Separate the chloro- 
form layer and add this to the main portion 
which contains nickel. 

4.3.2 Shake well ( 1-2 minutes ) the combined 
chloroform extract with two 5-ml portions of 
IN HCl and transfer both acid layers into a 
100-ml volumetric flask, dilute each flask to about 
50 ml with distilled water, add 1 ml of citric 
acid, 3 ml of potassium persulphate solution

15 ml 2M sodium hydroxide solution and 1 ml 
of dimethylglyoxime solution and mix. Heat 
to 60X in water bath and keep it at 60-70**C for 
5 minutes, cool and dilute to 100 ml with distill- 
ed water and mix. 

4«3.3 Measure absorbance after 10 minutes at 
a wavelength of 465 nm in I cm cell on a 
spectrophotometer. Run a blank using the same 
quantity of reagents except the nickel solution. 

4,3,4 Plot the photometric readings of calibra- 
tion solution against milligrams of nickel per 
100 ml of solution. 

5. PROCEDURE 

5.1 Ash 50 g of calcined petroleum coke sample 
after passing through 250-micron sieve in a 
porcelain dish at 950°C. Transfer the whole ash 
using camel hair brush to a platinum dish. 

5.2 Add 6 g of Na2C03 and 2*5 g of boric acid, 
mix thoroughly with glass rod, clean the glass 
rod with camel hair brush. Cover the dish with 
lid and heat slowly with burner for 10 minutes, 
avoid spurting, finally heat the dish in a muffle 



furnace at temperature of 950 ± 50**C for 30 
minutes. Take out the dish and cool. 

5.3 Extract the mass of the dish with 43 ml of 
8N HNO3, boil the solution for few minutes, 
cool and transfer into a 250-inl volumetric flask, 
make up to the mark with distilled water and 
mix. 

5.4 Take 10 ml aliquot from above solution 
( see 5.3 ) into a 250-ml beaker, add 5 ml of citric 
acid and proceed as in 4.3. 

5.5 Run a blank simultaneously through the 
entire procedure using all reagents and dilution 
exactly the same way excluding the sample. 

5.6 Measure the absorbance after 10 minutes at 
463 nm for the blank and sample. Deduct the 
reagent blank and calculate net milligrams of 
nickel ( Ni ) in the aliquot. 

6. CALCULATION 

6.1 Nickel ( Ni ) percent by mass = 
Net mg of Ni in aliquot X Aliquot factor X 100 
1 000 X mass of sample
